scope: Entity key extraction and read-side. extract_entity_keys(text) -> text[] derives entity keys from lesson text with deterministic shape rules (failure classes, model identifiers, source paths, schema-qualified names) — no LLM call, no external service. ingest() calls it and stores the result in metadata.entity_keys. recall_entity(entity_key, k) reads back everything held about one entity, keyed on metadata rather than on the heuristic content_type label. Additive: no table, column, or index definition changes to existing objects; no ranking or scoring change.
justification: Functional gate — no recall-quality metric is claimed, so no statistical validation is required. extract_entity_keys() is IMMUTABLE and pure; recall_entity() is a lookup keyed on metadata.entity_keys and does not touch recall_hybrid(), recall_fast(), recall_lessons(), RRF weights, confidence, or reinforce(). Density was measured before the read-side was built rather than assumed: on the active corpus (is_active AND t_valid_to = 'infinity', 5,910 lessons) extraction yields 972 distinct keys, median 2 lessons per key, 332 keys with three or more references — above the >1 median and >=20 dense-key thresholds set in the release plan. Both installcheck suites green.
schema_change_detail: No table, column, or index definition change. Two new functions (extract_entity_keys, recall_entity); ingest() body extended to populate metadata.entity_keys. Upgrade path: pgmnemo--0.15.1--0.16.0.sql. Fresh-install path: pgmnemo--0.16.0.sql.
scoring_impact: none — recall ranking, confidence, and reinforce() paths are untouched; no scoring coefficient changed
recall_ranking_impact: none — no change to result ordering, RRF weights, graph-proximity boost, recency stamping, or any GUC
backward_compat_proof: Existing callers see no change: no existing function signature, return shape, or default was modified. ingest() gains an additive metadata key (entity_keys); callers reading metadata by explicit key are unaffected. All 53 pre-existing extension tests and 9 pre-existing root tests continue to pass. One behaviour note for readers of the source: the schema: extraction rule was made deployment-agnostic before release — it previously matched a hardcoded allowlist of schema names, which meant it silently produced nothing on any other installation.
leak_scan: PASS — scripts/check_no_internal_leak.sh exit 0 (2026-07-31); the scan blocked an earlier candidate that hardcoded deployment-specific schema names, which was fixed before tagging
